This repairs the Rust cleanup against current main while preserving the newer bounded-source API and independent oracle expectations. It consolidates shared FENS verification and pinned SRS constants, preserves ledger refusal codes through SDK error wrapping, boxes large diagnostics/outcomes, and removes duplicate test-module mounts.

The integration restores both frozen normal-oracle JSON files to main's exact bytes. It also extends the ledger's declared source list to cover all 64 current Sherlock Rust files: the original 35 plus 29 added since the first PR candidate. The 61-file baseline and eight-file Core-stage append remain unchanged. Together with six declared backend paths, the list has 139 entries. These membership checks do not authenticate the complete Rust dependency graph or establish proof correctness.

The Rust workflow is manual only, matching the user's local-CI policy. Compile writes `source-projection.json` before the final `artifact.json` completion marker. Four incoming example binding-hash updates are retained but remain unvalidated by compiler/runtime execution. Source changes invalidate affected prior review, deployment and key identities; no keys or proof artifacts were regenerated.

Validation for this integrated candidate is limited to source inspection, Git/Python metadata checks and the recorded ten ordinary plugin-guidance tests. Independent ordinary and scoped security reviews are for draft source publication only. Cargo compilation, formatting, clippy, workspace tests and all native/SDK/proof/ledger checks remain UNRUN. The original author's macOS 890-test result belongs to the older `0861c75254f33b92194db0542f224215d47269a8` candidate and does not validate this integration. The user requested merge and fresh ordinary plus Opus 4.8 reviews approve source-only integration. Rust, native and ledger acceptance remain open.

The [doctorwatson<UTXO> / doctormoriarty<utxo> intake](https://github.com/CharlesHoskinson/Moriarty/blob/utxo/docs/utxo/doctorwatson/github/work-items.json) tracks this PR and issues #76–#89 against the applicable EARS and remaining checks. [Current publication receipts and review scope](https://github.com/CharlesHoskinson/Moriarty/blob/utxo/docs/utxo/doctorwatson/github/GITHUB-PUBLICATION.json) distinguish historical captures from later updates. Source publication does not close compiler, financial, proof or target-ledger requirements. Native authority remains zero; the broader Preprod goal remains paused.

Source-only merge disposition: ordinary Sherlock reporting QA passed 230 tests and plugin guidance passed 10. Cargo/Rust compilation and runtime tests, SDK/proof checks and ledger execution remain UNRUN. No native resource counter or EARS/product acceptance is reset. The optional SDK-linked Cargo test was not admitted by the security reviewer.

commits.messageBody:
Closes language-to-ledger task 5.1. Pins 121 constraints against recomputed
hashes across 37 source files and records 27 as explicit open items with true
reasons. The record declares itself incomplete, because it is.

Two review rounds. Round one returned BLOCKED, not for a fabricated value but
for over-caution: three open items claimed the repository did not determine a
value when it does, covering the Preview network tag and participant
identities, the lifecycle numeric target, and the set of contract addresses.
The reviewer looked specifically for an invented or inferred pin and found
none. The repair pinned what is determinable, corrected the false reasons and
narrowed two overstated wordings. Round two cleared all nine findings with no
new defects.

Four high-severity architectural findings are recorded and stand, each
confirmed by two independent readings. They are not fixed here, because none
of them can be fixed by a freeze:

- lenderCapability is declared and initialised in custody/loan.compact but no
  exported circuit takes a lender secret or asserts against it, while
  origination is a lender-to-debtor disbursement.
- The successor lifecycle state has exactly nine top-level keys and none is an
  authority, signature or nonce. Principal and accrued are real fields, but
  nested inside the obligation type.
- The lifecycle source declares exactly four operations, Transfer, Repay,
  Originate and Accrue. There is no fee operation and no outcome-intent
  authority, so the requirement that fees enter fee-inclusive net goals has no
  target in the source being lowered.
- The compiled ledger declarations carry no allowance or used-identifier
  fields, leaving replay defence on revision and kernel cursor alone.

The consequence is that task 5.1a cannot be executed as written: there is no
source-level slot to bind authority into and no fee operation to bind fees
into. Adding either changes the accepted source surface, which is a decision
for the repository owner, not for an implementation lane.

Satisfies only the first leg of open obligation 127, which forbids any retry
until there is a grounded change or proposal, fresh independent audits, and
root admission. This document is the proposal. It grants nothing and admits
nothing.

No K binary was executed and the retained diagnostic script was not run, since
running the frozen case is precisely what the obligation prohibits. Twenty
evidence hashes were recomputed independently with zero mismatches.

The proposal corrects a conflation that the orchestrating session introduced.
The two failures are distinct: macro05's own segmentation fault is inside the
LLVM interpreter at exit 113, while the kore-expand-macros segmentation fault
at exit 139 belongs to the earlier parse04 attempt.

That distinction matters for how the failure may be disposed of. Claim
CLM-0524, with its primary source in the pinned k-rust differential
configuration, corroborates parse04's kore-expand-macros crash as at minimum a
documented upstream exclusion class on the identical pinned K build 7.1.337.
It does not extend to macro05. So accepting the retained failure as a known
upstream exclusion is not available on this evidence.

macro05's cause remains undetermined between stack exhaustion and semantic
evaluation. Both the earlier diagnosis and this proposal conclude that telling
those apart needs a smallest-discriminator run, which has never been executed
and which nothing in the current budget can fund. Four options, an advisory
recommendation and six open questions are recorded for the owner.

Delivers the wrapper required by the afk-loan-executor specification under
"Prover lifetime established before daemon startup". An import-free static
executable runs as process one, parses and validates the six-line control
record, checks live boot and time-namespace identity, enforces the deadline as
min(entry+1500s, control deadline) on an absolute monotonic timer, forwards
termination signals with a two-second escalation grace, and reaps via the child
subreaper flag plus a bounded final sweep.

The control-record codec agrees byte for byte with the existing JavaScript
model. The test runs node at test time and compares against the C encoder on a
shared input rather than a stored copy. The model's source is embedded as a
fixture because it lives on a sibling branch; its sha256 a046a77a matches both
that worktree's file and the committed blob at cff5f1e3.

24 tests, all driven by real compiled child processes. Two create an actual
unprivileged user and PID namespace and prove a process-group-detached
descendant dies on namespace teardown, both when the supervisor exits cleanly
and when it is killed abruptly.

Independently audited, verdict APPROVED, nine findings with none blocking and
none above medium. The auditor established the tests are load-bearing by
replacing the source with an empty main, which failed 23 of 24, and by injecting
twelve compiling mutants, of which ten were killed by targeted tests. It
confirmed the namespace test with a positive control, measured the deadline
holding at 0.98s against 1.0s under a signal storm, and reproduced the build
byte-identically.

Three items the audit left open for a follow-up round: the subreaper claim is
not proved by its test, because the grandchild dies via its process group
regardless; the exit-code table implies 124 is reserved while a child exiting
124, 64, 125 or 126 is propagated unchanged; and the build document omits its
toolchain version and expected digest.

No Python file under scripts/moriarty_dev changed, so the hook digest pin is
undisturbed and tool interception is unaffected.

Implements the remaining scoped requirement of the afk-loan-executor
specification's "Concrete one-shot runner invocation handoff": an AF_UNIX socket
in a restricted runtime directory, a 256-bit nonce compared in constant time,
the two invocation environment values set explicitly rather than inherited, peer
credential retrieval, bounded process ancestry, exactly-one-handshake
enforcement, a durable invocation event written before the handshake is
answered, and EOF before setup distinguished from EOF after startup.

A first round enforced the one-shot rule only by closing the connection, so a
replay produced a broken pipe on the client write and the test failed on an
unhandled error. That was the rule being unavailable rather than enforced. The
replay is now refused explicitly: the server returns HANDOFF_REPLAY_DENIED,
records the denial durably before answering, and the test asserts the denial
payload, the record, and the ordering of record-start, record-done and
denial-received, plus that confirm and response each ran exactly once so no
state or response work repeated. The rule is now observable and distinguishable
from the other denial cases.

28 tests in the handoff suite, all passing. Every midnight suite is clean: 52,
576, 3, 11, 27, 89 and 52, re-run by the orchestrator rather than taken from the
lane report. No existing test was weakened; the corrected expectation asserts the
specified refusal instead of tolerating an unhandled write error.

The executor caller, fault matrix and prover-lifetime model are carried here from
the audited round that introduced them, byte-identical to the approved versions.

commits.messageBody:
Implements the scoped requirement of the afk-loan-executor specification's
"Concrete one-shot runner invocation handoff": an AF_UNIX socket in a 0700
runtime directory with the socket at 0600, a 32-byte nonce compared with
timingSafeEqual, the two invocation environment values set explicitly as the
child's entire environment with process.env never spread, peer credential
retrieval, bounded process ancestry with retained start ticks, exactly-one
handshake, a durable invocation event appended before the handshake is answered,
and EOF before setup distinguished from EOF after startup.

History, stated accurately. Round one's test already demanded the replay denial
code and already failed. Round one's implementation did send a denial, but
synchronously on connection before reading, so the client's in-flight write hit
EPIPE. Round two waits for the peer's first data before recording and answering.
The expectation was raised, never relaxed.

Independently audited, verdict WARNING. What the audit established: the denial
has a single producer, the one-shot guard; the protocol details are real and
mutation-detected; the environment is genuinely closed; and 31 of 31 tests are
load-bearing under 41 mutations, of which 31 were detected.

Three things this commit does not claim, correcting an earlier draft of this
message which got two of them wrong:

- executor-caller.mjs and its test are NOT byte-identical to the approved
  cff5f1e3. They changed, from 2d614732 to ac87dccb and 4d53e804 to c85f0ff9.
  The change is a necessary improvement over a placeholder, but it was not
  carried over unmodified and should not have been described that way.
  fault-matrix.mjs and prover-lifetime.mjs are genuinely unchanged.
- The record-before-answer ordering is real at the code level by construction,
  but its test assertion is not load-bearing: reversing the implementation to
  write bytes before awaiting the record leaves all tests passing, because the
  recorder resolves before socket data reaches the client.
- Of the scenario's seven denial cases, four are enforced and mutation-detected:
  forged nonce, authority, launcher identity and replay. Reservation and stale
  store event are pass-through, where the test supplies the error whose message
  becomes the code, so the module enforces ordering rather than the predicate.
  Boot mismatch has no denial path at all: the comparator exists and no caller
  converts a false result into a denial.

Two open high-severity items for the next round. A connection race: the socket
listens before spawn but the connection handler attaches only after the durable
append, so a child connecting inside that window is dropped, yielding a spurious
setup timeout and then an orphaned accepted socket that prevents server close
from calling back, so the executor never returns. Measured at a 60ms append with
an immediate connect. And the boot-mismatch denial path above.

Implements roadmap task 5.1a, which could not be done as written because the
reviewed constraint freeze established there was nowhere to bind to: the lender
capability was never asserted by any circuit, the lifecycle state had no
authority slot, and the profile declared no fee operation.

Additive versioning throughout, with every prior version still accepted and no
exported name removed: source profile 5 to 6, Core contract 4 to 5, lifecycle
state 1 to 2, kernel 1 to 2. The lender capability is now asserted in exactly one
circuit, the disbursing one, over a capability hash binding the role domain,
network tag, program digest and lender secret. A Fee operation joins the four
existing ones, and the fee-inclusive net-goal rule from the freeze is enforced.

Independently audited, verdict WARNING. The question that could have blocked it
came back clean: the source rule and the compiled circuit are exact algebraic
mirrors including refusal codes, verified across eleven edge cases and
corroborated empirically at the boundary where a fee of one versus two flips the
outcome. The auditor widened the byte check to all 38 freeze-pinned paths with
zero drift, and found 26 of 28 new tests load-bearing.

Three findings recorded, one substantive. The capability assertion proves the
lender knows the secret; it does not make the lender the funder, and nothing
debits the borrower, so amounts are constrained while party attribution is not.
The implementer disclosed that itself as an open item. Second, the conditional
assertion in the generated contract was the only one of its kind in the
repository, with no compiled precedent. Third, roughly 3236 of about 3300 new
runtime lines duplicate existing files where neighbouring versions use short
re-export shims.

Task 5.2a is included: the generated contract compiles under the pinned Compact
0.31.1 toolchain, producing TypeScript bindings, a zkir circuit for origination
and compiler metadata, all retained with hashes bound to the contract source, the
generator and the lifecycle source. That settles the conditional-assertion risk
by evidence rather than argument. Proof keys were skipped, so this is not a
proving build and establishes no Docker, Preview or financial outcome.

Gap four is declined and remains open: allowances and the four replay registers
still have no on-ledger counterpart, which needs a ledger schema change.

An earlier attempt edited the retained generator, which is itself pinned in a
required-sources manifest compared against the retained build receipt, and broke
three suites. It was reverted and the emitter moved to a new file. Both the
failing and repaired outputs are retained as evidence.

Captures the working-tree state so nothing exists only on one machine. This is
preservation, not reviewed delivery. Three kinds of content, and the distinction
matters:

Plugin runtime, authored earlier in the session and already in force. Adds
bootstrap.py and deployment.py, updates compatibility.py and hook_protocol.py,
and replaces the hook registrations with a pinned-runtime launcher that verifies
a SHA-256 digest over every Python file under scripts/moriarty_dev before running,
failing closed on a mismatch. The digest is consistent: it appears four times in
hooks.json and recomputes to the same value from the tree. Any future edit to
those files must re-pin in the same change, or every hook degrades and tool
interception stops.

K diagnostic work in progress: the macro05 trace106 diagnostic with its pins,
ownership, host evidence path and snapshot, retained unchanged as evidence.

Session evidence: closure receipts for roadmap section 0 and task 5.1, the
executor verification record, the AFK handover, sprint and model-docs
deliverables, the session-completion-sprints package, and the roadmap checkbox
state for the two closed sections.

Excluded after a credential scan. Eleven tracked files carried credential-shaped
strings and are not present: five Gemini documentation page dumps, which embed
Google's own public devsite keys and were never added here; three Cake
working-group page dumps, one of which also carried an AWS access key identifier;
a NEAR tutorial containing an ed25519 private key string from its own worked
example; and a GitHub API response dump. All were third-party scraped web content.
No credential belonging to this project was present: the scan specifically
covered private key blocks, service account JSON, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI,
Slack and Stripe tokens, AWS secrets, Cardano extended signing keys and seed
phrases, and found none.

Two scan patterns produced only false positives and are recorded so nobody
re-raises them: matches beginning sk- were documentation anchor slugs and package
names, and a twelve-word mnemonic pattern matched ordinary English prose.

The six pre-existing files are deleted going forward. They remain in this
repository's earlier history, so a full purge would require a history rewrite on
a public remote, which is a separate decision.

Also removes a stray agent worktree of 18,619 files left under .claude/ by one of
this session's audit agents. It was registered, locked and clean, and has been
unregistered rather than committed.

commits.messageBody:
Design and research for a high-level Moriarty language, its reduction to a small
core, and how that core could reach the Midnight circuit IR. Planning only: no
product code changes, nothing ticked, no admission granted.

## Surface language

Three independent designs against a measured problem. The loan lifecycle example
is 178 lines of which 13 are logic; 80 restate emit fields, 46 declare records
and 39 are ensures, most of them stating what does not change. The rewrite is 72
lines, measured.

Two features survived a deliberate test against novelty. Asset-scoped precision,
where a declared scale plus a bare literal resolves by expected type while the
unit vector survives into the elaborated form. And phase-typed state, where the
ensure block sees a different type than the body, making the soundness property
unforgeable by spelling rather than enforced by a scope rule. Party identity was
explicitly rejected as a novelty claim: it is an enumerated type.

The binding rule throughout, taken from what o1js gets wrong: no sugar may
introduce a spelling that is both shorter and less sound than what it replaces.

## Core reduction

Sixty constructors reduce to roughly fifteen, analysed in three disjoint slices.
The count is an estimate, not a verified result, and the reconciliation note in
docs/design records why: two shared formers are unowned, Select and case were
never checked for identity, the two keyed lookups vanish if state is modelled as
a bounded value, and neither minimality nor completeness was proved. The real
range is about fourteen to eighteen, driven by decisions nobody has taken.

Three findings a naive reading of Simplicity would have missed. The work meter is
observable, so a jet's cost must be declared rather than derived. A static rule
requires an operand to be syntactically a literal, which blocks hash-recognised
jets outright. And a jet needs a lower definition to be identical to, so jets
follow a backend rather than precede it.

Load-bearing correction: Core contains no hash, curve or commitment constructor.
That matters more than the count, because a cryptographic primitive is exactly
the obligation automated field reasoning cannot discharge.

## Compilation path

There is no compiler from Core to Compact today. What exists is a validator that
rejects any source whose digest is not one pinned constant, plus Compact
assembled from JavaScript template literals. The file says so itself.

Recommended: a credible compiler with a verified checker. The lowerer emits the
simulation relation alongside each contract; a small checker, proven once,
discharges the obligations. Rejected: full compiler verification, at 42,000 lines
of Coq and three person-years for CompCert; black-box validation, which tops out
at 80-97% of functions and has never faced a target whose meaning is witness
existence; and formalising a Compact subset, because every mechanisation in the
JSCert lineage died at the standard it started with, and Compact changed the ZKIR
representation of conditional branches with no syntax change at all.

## Corrections recorded against my own earlier claims

Totality does not shrink the checkers' undecided bucket. Circom templates are
unrolled before Picus or AC-4 see them, so those tools already consume the
finite, loop-free systems a total language produces; their wall is Groebner
blow-up, not undecidability. What totality does buy is that the per-constructor
strategy is viable and that the coinductive half of the two-language equivalence
proof system is never invoked.

K has no native support for relating two definitions. The tool that did, keq, was
added in 2018 and deleted in 2023 with the Java backend, and nothing replaced it.

The ZKIR K semantics is 4,969 lines on the r3-native worktree, not the 2,815 I
first quoted from the copy under graphs/.

## Cautions carried forward

Marlowe's mechanised money-preservation theorem was wrong until a 2023 audit: it
ignored token type, so a contract swapping twenty of one asset for fifteen of
another passed in both directions. A machine-checked proof of the wrong property
is the failure mode to fear here.

Of ninety-five surveyed under-constrained bugs, thirty-four are a call site
failing to discharge a correct gadget's precondition, so composition is an
obligation rather than a consequence.

Six research reports with retrieved sources and URLs are under
deliverables/research-2026-09-13/, each flagging what it could not retrieve.

Bring the crates added since the beta toolchain back in line with
RUST_GUIDELINES.md and make main green under cargo fmt, clippy and test.

Errors and dependencies
- Drop anyhow from mori-ledger. Its ProvingProvider impl now names the
  SDK's own ProvingError alias, and prove_prepared_call recovers the
  prover's refusal (snapshot-key-location, binding-changed-activity,
  proving-activity-mismatch) through the SDK's TransactionProvingError
  wrapping instead of reporting every failure as sdk-intent-proving.
- Declare midnight-curves and midnight-proofs in [workspace.dependencies]
  and group the workspace dependencies.
- Box the optional diagnostics on mori-ledger's Error, the large
  SegmentRun and LoadedAuthorization variants, and fix the remaining
  clippy warnings so clippy passes with -D warnings.

Duplication
- mori-ledger now depends on mori-backend and reuses its FENS Schnorr
  verifier (wrapped in ledger refusal codes), pinned SRS hashes and byte
  cap. mori-backend uses mori-core's hex. The ledger notice points at the
  shared verifier and still covers constraints.rs.
- Mount mori-ledger's test support and Sherlock's extra oracle programs
  once instead of loading each file as several modules.

Tests that were failing on main (19)
- Add the 35 Sherlock sources and the reused backend files to the ledger
  source closure, and match excluded files by whole path component.

commits.messageBody:
Agents working in crates/ had no instruction to read RUST_GUIDELINES.md:
neither AGENTS.md nor the moriarty-dev plugin mentioned it.

- RUST_GUIDELINES.md gains the rules recent changes broke without them
  being written down: everything builds and tests through Cargo (no
  direct-rustc harness, no #[path] remounts), no test-only prototypes in
  src/, no identities hashed from source text, no absolute paths, no
  anyhow in library crates, the fmt/clippy/test gates, justified
  #[allow]s, and comments that explain code rather than process.
- The develop skill points Rust changes at the guidelines and a new
  references/rust.md checklist. Deviations need the maintainer's
  agreement, the three cargo checks pass before handoff, and reviewers
  check conformance.
- AGENTS.md gets a Rust toolchain section saying the same, so agents
  that skip the plugin still see it.
- Plugin version 0.1.2; the guidance tests cover the new checklist.
